subject: Transformers Mellum2 and Mellum2.1 native MTP contract intake
findings: Mellum aliases num_mtp_layers to num_nextn_predict_layers, permits at most one layer, and defaults that layer to sliding attention plus sparse MoE.

The merged upstream schema stores fusion and post-normalization tensors at mtp.fc, mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding, mtp.pre_fc_norm_hidden and mtp.norm; its sparse predictor block is source layer 28 and shares the target embedding and LM head.

The MTP layer concatenates normalized next-token embeddings before normalized target final-norm hidden state, applies the learned 2H-to-H projection, then one private sliding-attention sparse-MoE block and post norm.
The locally recorded Mellum2.1 artifact declares no MTP layer and contains no MTP tensors, so it cannot load, qualify or select this route.
The PR index was fresh at 2026-10-15T21:10:33Z: Transformers #49531 and #49544 were merged, but neither publishes trained Mellum MTP weights.
modifications: Added an adapter-owned exact future-artifact schema for one source-layer-28 sliding-attention sparse-MoE head, including projection order, shared tensors, private cache identity and strict incomplete/wrong-layer refusal.
Added the one-layer fusion, predictor block, private rotating-KV state, shared target projection and mtp_step component behind the existing ordinary-only adapter gate.

Kept ordinary decode unchanged and the MTP capability absent. Even a synthetically complete index is refused until trained weights receive real-artifact reference parity and serving rollback/APCv2 validation.
CPU tests compare fusion against an independent NumPy reference and verify full speculative rollback followed by width-one recomputation preserves exact cache and continuation logits.
